correctness.rationale: A deterministic program reconstructs the bipartite Kneser graph on 20 vertices and 30 edges and all 6,211 nonempty independent simplices. An augmented 3,103-pair discrete-Morse matching is proved acyclic on every one of 30,380 Hasse incidences; its only critical cells are one in dimension four and five in dimension five, and every integral Morse differential coefficient is computed to be zero. Consequently reduced integral homology is free of ranks 1 and 5. Group actions from five-label permutations and set complement produce 240 distinct automorphisms; independent all-automorphism backtracking finds exactly 240. For every automorphism, two independent algorithms agree on signed reduced Lefschetz values. The formula L(pc^e)=(-1)^e(sgn(p)-fixed_points(p)) is exhaustively verified and the character-inner-product argument forces the claimed two degree-wise rational G-modules. Exact finite checks are reproduced from the enclosed program; other particle numbers and integral degree-five G-lattice are not inferred.

originality.rationale: The classification is the full rational S5 x C2 action on degree-four and degree-five independence homology of the Desargues graph, not a new assertion about the already known Betti numbers or wedge type. Full published result statements for the exact graph have only the nonequivariant wedge. Relevant foundational and incidence-graph general theorems do not evaluate this automorphism representation; the complete character, including the central complement sign, was not found in the searched records. Originality remains a best-evidence finding rather than a guarantee of global priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivariant computation or an unstated specialization of a stronger representation theorem could imply the character; publication priority remains uncertain.
The 2017 incidence-graph reduction is natural for some symmetries and could simplify derivation, but its full text does not give the 14-class character or the complement-exchange action.
The degree-five integral automorphism lattice is not classified, and is not claimed as part of the result.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a canonical, highly symmetric 20-vertex bipartite Kneser graph with full 240-element automorphism group. Its independence homotopy has adjacent nonzero dimensions, and its degree-wise equivariant homology is not implied by known Betti numbers. The signed 5-point permutation representation is a complete natural invariant for this graph, distinguishes the effect of the central complement involution from the S5-fixed line, and can be used in equivariant topology of bipartite incidence graphs. The finite scope is motivated by the graph and symmetry, not by an arbitrary parameter slice; there is no claim of downstream family theorem.
